DearStudents, Why do we study and practice art? Such questions arise from the common perception that art is an "innate talent." However, just like any other field of humanities, the study of art also demands our attention and intellect. This textbook, which focuses on areas like visual art, sculpture, music, dance, drama, and cinema, goes beyond mere knowledge acquisition in these subjects. It aims to encourage creative activities related to these artforms. Beyond the conventional method of practicing any art form with a competitive mindset, this textbook aspires to revitalize the educational process creatively by fostering a deep understanding of all art forms.

Through this book, we delve into various timeless aspects of visual arts, cinema, dance, music, theater, and more. In that sense, it serves as an entry way to an expansive creative world.Explore,discover,sing,act,and immerse yourselves in joy.We eagerly look forward to your feedback and suggestions. This textbook is designed in such a way to understand art through activities. The art education textbook aims at the all-round personality development of children, like having an exemplary perspective in the approach to the surroundings and fellow beings, acquiring skills and knowledge in such a way as to be able to create and share innovative thoughts that will strengthen the society, and nurturing creative abilities and finding their own place in the society. For that purpose, five fields, namely painting and sculpture, music, drama, cinema and dance, are included in this textbook. That's why various projects have been included in this textbook considering the taste of each of you, the fields of study required by the period, and the future career prospects. By preparing these projects you can go far in your field of interest.

Along with this textbook, the projects are planned to make the most of the knowledge and experiences you have gained from the art education lessons from class five to nine. Projects are included in the six chapters of this textbook in the areas of painting, sculpture, music, drama, cinema and dance, with the aim of nurturing your sense of inquiry and research aptitude. A total of three projects, one per term, should be submitted in an academic year. The project structure and general guidelines are given in the introduction. Other suggestions according to the characteristics of each project, the learning activities leading to it, etc. are included in the respective lessons. The pages provided at the end of the book shall be used for planning the selected projects. You can also seek help from parents, teachers, friends and experts related to your chosen field to prepare the project.
The ultimate goal of the art education textbook is to create an "art literate new generation".

Baul Music Baul is a significant genre in Indian folk music culture, which is popular in West Bengal, Bangladesh, Tripura, Assam and Meghalaya. It is a continuation of the devotional poetry movement of medieval India. This includes the melodies that indicate human love and their connection with nature. There are so many Baul songs under Boudha- Vaishnava- Tantric categories. Most of the existing Baul songs were written by Lalon Fakir, the famous Baul poet. Regional musical instruments like ektara, dotara, duggi, flute, hand bells, and ankle bells are integral components. Ektara Ektara is an ancient string instrument in India. Baul singers use to play ektara in accompaniment to the song. It is popular in the Indian states like Bengal and Rajasthan, and countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh. The name ektara originated because of it’s single string. There is also its two stinged variety. It is called dotara/dutara.

Ritualistic Steps Kerala’s performing arts could be categorised as ritualistic and recreational, based on the performance contexts. The art forms performed in ritualistic contexts are known as ritual arts. Eg- Theyyam, Thira, Mudiyettu, Padayani, Rathib etc. Art forms performed for entertainment purposes are known as recreational arts. Eg- Kolkali, Kakkarassinatakam etc. Let’s Find Out Identify and list out the ritual and recreational regional art forms that are practised now, or that were practised once and became extinct. Based on form and structure, folk performing arts could be divided into folk dance and folk drama. Folk dance comprises rhythmic steps and body movements. Folk dramas are art forms that narrate some incidents or stories.

Art forms like Theyyam, Thira, Mudiyettu, Ninabali and Chavittu Natakam have more dramatic elements, and those like Thidambu Nritham, Kolkkali, Chavittu Kali, Kalattakkali, Chozhikali, Thiruvathira, Dafmuttu and Margam Kali have more dance elements.

A Vibrant Society with Better Mental Health You have learnt about dimensions of health such as physical health and emotional health in the previous classes. Shall we get familiarised with the other two dimensions - mental health and social health? Let us start with a real - life incident Arunima Sinha was a national volleyball player. On 12th April 2011, while trying to rescue her fellow passengers, Arunima was thrown off board a train by a group of bandits. The accident cost her left leg which was amputated at the young age of 26. Later, a prosthetic leg (artificial leg) was implanted, so that Arunima could return to her normal life. While under treatment, she decided to scale Mount Everest drawing inspiration from Yuvraj Singh who had fought malignancy (cancer) and returned to international cricket. She got

the foundational training for mountaineering with the assistance provided by Nehru Institute of Mountaineering, Uttarkashi and Bachendri Pal, who had conquered Mount Everest. First Aid measures for an Electric Shock 1. We should ensure personal safety and safety of those around us. 2. Don’t touch the victim of an electric shock directly. If we touch them, we may also be electrocuted since the victim may still be in contact with the electric current. 46 Health and Physical Education

3. Either disconnect the electric connection or block its source. If you cannot disconnect the electric connection, use a dry twig or things like rubber gloves which are bad conductors of electricity, to detach the victim from the source of the shock. 4. Ask the victim if everything is okay (Are you ok?) by patting on the shoulder to test whether the person is responding or not. 5. If visible burns are there, pour cold water on the wound continuously for 10 minutes. Avoid using ice or water that is extremely cold. This may lead to damage of tissues. 6. Cover the burnt area with a sterile bandage. Avoid using objects like cotton that may be sticky. 7. If the victim does not respond, he/she may be in an unconscious state. Check the breathing of the victim. If breathing has stopped, dial '112' to avail emergency service and medical care. Ensure personal medical assistance along with that.
If an accident victim does not breathe, provide CPR. Continue CPR until emergency medical service arrives.
Steps involved in CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) 1. Make the victim lie in supine position in a safe place. 2. Check the breathing of the victim. Activity book 47

3. Check the pulse of the victim. 4. Before providing CPR, open the mouth of the victim and ensure that there is no object that obstructs the passage of air. 5. Keep one palm on the middle part of the chest of the victim. Keep the next palm over it, and clasp them together. Keep the arms and shoulders of the caregiver at an angle of 90 degrees and compress the victim’s chest 30 times. For children who are below the age of one year, pressure should be applied using the index and middle finger. 6. The rate of chest compression shall be 100 times per minute. Compression should be 2 inches deep. 7. Tilt the head backwards and lift the chin. 8. Covering the nose, give rescue breaths twice, at the ratio of one per second. Check whether the chest of the victim is rising and falling. 9. After this, repeat the activity of chest compression 30 times. 10. Ensure the use of Automatic External Defibrillator (AED), if it is available.
AED is a machine that helps to check and regulate the heart rate, if needed. 48 Health and Physical Education

There are vertically and horizontally running threads. The threads at the edge of the cloth are seen very close. (Pic 2.2) Pic 2.2 The thread that runs lengthwise through the fabric is known as wrap. Towards the edges the warps appear very close to each other. The finished edge of fabric is called selvedge. The threads that run across the warps over and under the lengthwise threads are called weft. (Pic.2.2) Can you identify the warp and weft observing the clothes in your hand? Take the cloth and pull it to different directions. Do you feel the pulls going in the same directions? When the edge of the cloth is pulled, the part of warp remains firm whereas threads bend when pulled. Warp is stronger than weft.

The direction in which the warp and weft is arranged in a cloth is called grain. The direction in which the warp passes through is called straight grain and the direction in which weft passes through is called cross grain. Any direction between the straight grain and the cross grain is called bias direction. True bias is the direction that runs at 45 degree angle between straight grain and cross grain. Try to understand more about the direction of clothes with the help of the picture 2.3

We are familiar with buildings used for various purposes like houses, schools and shopping malls etc. As per the National Building Code, buildings are classified into nine categories.

Pic 1.4 • Group-A : Residential Building - Residential buildings like house, hostel etc. • Group-B : Educational Building- Buildings used for educational purposes. • Group-C : Institutional Building - Buildings used for health and medical purposes. • Group-D : Assembly Building - Buildings used for assembly of a group of people for various purposes.

• Group-E : Business Building - Buildings used for commercial purposes with proper record keeping. • Group F : Mercantile Building - Buildings used for business purposes. • Group G : Industrial Building - Buildings used for any type of production. • Group-H : Storage Building- Buildings where various types of goods are stored. • Group -J : Hazardous Building- Buildings used for handling unsafe materials Activity 1 Complete the table given below. 10 House Residential building Hospital School Bakery Bank We have understood that permission should be obtained before construction of building. What are we familiar with, in the above given figure? • • You are already familiar with plan and front elevation. Now what is a section? A section is a cross section of a building. The height and depth of the building and the details of construction materials used are obtained from the section drawing. Pic 1.13

A cross section is shown in the picture to help you understand what the different parts of the building are. Let’s see what some of the main parts are and their function. 1. Foundation : The lowest part of the building. The entire weight of the building is transferred to the ground. 2. Basement (Plinth): The part between ground level and ground floor level. The ground floor level helps to rise the building above the ground. 3. Wall: Helps to secure the building and separate the interior space into different rooms. 4. Lintel : Lintel is situated over the openings like door, window etc. It closes them, helping in construction at the top and in the transfer of the weight to the bottom. 5. Roof: The topmost part of the building. Its function is to protect it from weather changes.

Service plan is another important document to be submitted for getting building permission. It does not include terraces, common areas, lifts, corridors, utility ducts etc. Pic 1.15 Let’s see how we can find out the floor area and plinth area of a building if we get a plan with measurements.

The world of Ornamental Plants Let's familiarise the ornamental plants that we grow in the premises of our garden and home. Ornamental plants are the plants that we grow to make our environment beautiful. These are plants mainly grown for flowers, leaves, fragrance and appearance. They not only enhance the beauty of the home, but also make the

garden, park and business centres attractive. Flowers of different colours and shapes, leaves, branches etc enrich the beauty of nature. Characteristics of ornamental plants We have understood that the ornamental plants are different from other plants. Let us examine the uses of ornamental plants. 1. Beautification: Ornamental plants help to enhance the aesthetic value of environment. Flowers of different colours and shapes turn to be mind blowing sights. 2. Environmental protection: Ornamental plants purify air and provides environmental protection.

3. Mental Health: The presence of plants makes the mind calm and helps to improve mental health. The main purpose is to improve the mental and physical health through activities engaging in planting, growing and caring of plants. Species of Ornamental plants on the flower map Before starting gardening, let us identify the ornamental plants grown in gardens and home and their characteristics. The most common ornamental plants are flowering plants such as rose, jasmine, chrysanthemum, hibiscus, ixora etc.

Foliage plants are the plants that are grown for attractive colour and shape of leaves. Croton, marantha, dieffenbachia, money plant belongs to this category. Some of the above plants complete their life cycle in one year or one season. Marigold, balsam, gomphrena, cosmos, celosia, etc are the annuals belonging to this category. These plants are propagated by seeds. Cassia, Ashoka tree, hibiscus, nerium, tabernaemontana have more than two years of life span. They are called perennials. Ornamental plants differ in their growth characteristics also. Marigold, balsam, portulaca, zinnia, etc are soft stemmed herbs. Perennial shrubs grow to a height of one metre to four metre. Among these hibiscus, rose, nerium, crossandra etc are grown for flowers while croton, phyllanthus, dracaena, etc are grown for the beauty of their leaves.

Flower that follows the direction of Sun: Some flowers follow the direction of Sun. This phenomenon is called heliotropism. The plants such as adenium, hoya, aloevera which store water in their leaves and stem can be included in the category of Cactii and Succulents. Tube roses, lilies etc are bulbous plants having underground stem. Lotus and water lilies are aquatic plants. Cactus Cactii have long thorns instead of leaves. These structures reduce the loss of water due to heat and protect the plant. Succulents can store water in their fleshy stems, leaves and roots. The cactus has not only thorns but also flowers. Some succulents have a lifespan of more than 100 years, especially agave and century plant which sustain centuries. Climbers such as jasmine, money plant, bougainvillea, clitoria need a support 14 or assistance to climb. Synconium, morning glory, wandering jew etc which grow on the ground are creepers . Red palm, yellow palm, fishtail palm etc are palms and the plants such as nephrolepis which propagates through spores are called ferns.

UNIT Garden Components : The Attraction of the Garden Gardens are aesthetically designed spaces that gives peace, relaxation entertainment and experience to the sightseers and visitors. Gardening is the practice of planting and caring ornamental plants in an attractive and artistic way, combining science and art. Gardening is a source of entertainment, pleasure and relaxation for an individual and society. Landscaping is the art of designing a garden. The person who does landscaping is known as a landscaper. A site selected for setting up the garden is just like a canvas to a landscaper. Differently coloured plants and other materials in the garden are its colours. There are different components that give special beauty to the garden. They are called garden components. These elements provide beauty to the garden and make it attractive and give good experience to the viewers. Let us familiarise with them. Activity 1

Given below are two different pictures of the famous Rashtrapati Bhavan garden in Delhi, the capital of our country. Observe the picture and make a list of various components that made the garden beautiful. Pic 2.1 Pic 2.2

1. Flower beds 2. Pathways 3. ............................ 4. ............................ 5. ............................ 6. ............................ Garden components Along with the plant components, non -plant components also play a major role in making a garden beautiful. Let's familiarise different garden components. Plant components : Garden components made by using various plants are called plant components. 1. Arches Arches are the welcome gate of a garden. These are 18 used as the main entrance of a garden or as a way to enter into a specific area. Arches can be made using trees, metals, concrete, bamboo etc. Pic 2.3 (Arches)

2. Pergola Pergolas are extended arches made up of consecutive arches. Pergolas are used for creating an exhibition in the garden. This is like a beautiful roof covered with climbers, through which air and light can pass. Often they can be built above garden benches, shady walkways, common areas etc. Pergolas can be made up of trees, metals, concrete and bamboo. Pic 2.4 (Pergola)

3. Carpet Bed Carpet beds are designed using low growing foliage and flowering plants. They are mainly used for constructing logos, name boards and symbols of institutions. Plants of different colours and shapes are used for making this. 4. Hedges and Edges Hedges are created by growing plants as short Pic 2.5 (Carpet Bed) walls or boundaries. Shrubs having small leaves are more suitable for this. Hedges are plants that increases the scenic beauty of the garden. Edges are used for separating garden pathways, lawns and other components. Plants having small leaves and pebbles are used for making edge. Dwarf shrubs which are low growing are used for making edges. Pic 2.6 (Hedge) Pic 2.7 (Edge) 5. Lawn Lawns are small areas in the garden where grasses are cut and trimmed for attraction and entertainment. Lawns are described as the heart of the garden. PIc 2.8 (Lawn)

6. Shrubbery Shrubbery is an area where foliage and flowering shrubs are grown together. They give attraction and beauty to the garden. Rosary or Rosarium is a collection of different coloured roses which are grown together. Pic 2.9 (Shrubbery) 7. Topiary Topiary is the art of pruning plants to different shapes. Topiary is transforming plants into creatures, objects and various shapes by trimming. Eg: Phyllanthus Pic 2.10 (Topiary) 8. Trophy Trophy is the method of decorating plants in attractive layers around a central object like flag post, statue, lantern etc. Pic 2.11 (Trophy) 9. Flower beds Growing of flowering annuals and perennials in groups are called flower beds. Flower beds create wonder or interest in the eyes of the viewers. Pic 2.11 (Flower beds) These can be grown around the walkways, lawns

and around foundation of houses. Annuals like Zinnia, Chinese Balsam, Daisy etc are suitable for this. 10. Rock Garden Rock Garden is the uneven arrangement of rocks and stones in the open spaces of the garden for maintaining originality. Pic 2.12 (Rock Garden) 11. Water garden or Aquatic Garden Water garden or Aquatic garden is a small pond or stream built in the garden for growing aquatic plants and fishes. Catchy areas in the garden or natural sunken areas having small pond can be converted into water garden. 21 Non -plant components Non- plant components are artificial constructions Pic 2.13(Water garden) that enhance the beauty of the garden along with the plant components. 1. Walkway 2. Fountains 3. Garden Benches 4. Statues 5. Streams 6. Fancy lamps 7. Bird Bath Similar components provide beauty and attraction Pic 2.14 to the garden.

Other Features of Garden Components Climbers : Apart from providing beauty, climbers hinder cool breeze and retain heat. In some areas climbers are grown around buildings to regulate temperature. Trees : Each tree creates a ‘micro climate’, that is, a constant temperature and coolness is maintained in the area where the tree is located. In addition, some trees reduce the pH of the soil and provide a nutrient - rich environment for the surrounding plants. Lawns : Lawns help to set the climate of the nature. They helps to reduce heat, attract dust and conserve rain water.

Bonsai: The World of Dwarf Trees Let's familiarize another art form which is maintained 22 in many gardens. Whenever big trees are seen, you are attracted by their shapes and structures, aren’t you? But do you know that these trees can be kept in shallow containers in your home after making it in dwarf form? That is Bonsai. Bonsai is a Japanese word. It means ‘the tree in a shallow container.’ Although it began very earlier in China, Pic 2.14 Bonsai became world famous as part of Japanese culture. Bonsai maintenance is both an art and a science. As it requires, caring and accuracy for growing, like a large tree. For giving special shapes and beauty to the bonsai plant, timely cutting and pruning is essential. Ficus, pine, bougainvillea, tamarind etc are good for making bonsai. You can also grow a bonsai! If you have a bonsai, it will be a life lesson; a lesson of patience and respect to nature.

General Principles to follow in Gardening Now we are going to tell about how to make a beautiful garden using ornamental plants. When you start making the garden, you have to give attention to the following things. Basic knowledge about plants A thorough understanding of the classification and growth habit of each plant. Design of the Garden Design the garden in such a way that the owner’s preferences are reflected. At home or in a public place, access the size of the construction site, surroundings, availability of water, topography etc Integration with the Garden Surrounding Plants should not be just planted, but should be in such a way as to enhance the beauty of the surroundings. Building and garden should be harmoniously united in appearance. Planting according to the classification of plants Grow flowers and plants in different groups. Use trees like Polyalthia to give variety in corners.

Sense of Equality Surroundings, plants and trees should give a sense of equality. Fruit plants and ornamental plants should be represented in large gardens. Importance of Lawns The lawn in front of a building enhances beauty. Avoiding of paths, if not necessary, will give more beauty. Natural Beauty Try to maintain natural beauty and make the area enjoyable to all.

UNIT Garden Making Pic 3.1 What comes to your mind when you think of a garden? Isn't it a peaceful and green place full of beautiful flowers? A garden is not only a beautiful place but also a place that teaches us about nature. Garden making is one of the most interesting activities. Now let's see how to make a garden according to the availability of space and situation. Although creating an ornamental garden is an act that requires a lot of attention and designing, the result of the effort is that beautiful gardens can be established in homes, schools and public streets.

Environmental benefits The presence of garden improves air quality, increases oxygen production and decrease carbon dioxide levels. It also helps to maintain a greater bond with nature. Different types of tools are needed to grow and maintain plants well in the garden. Each tool has its specific use. So understanding about them is helpful for proper maintenance. Some important garden tools are given below: 1. Spade It is an important tool used for ploughing, weeding and breaking clods. It helps to manage soil easily. 2. Garden Shears Pic 3.2 Garden Shears are used to remove unwanted leaves and stem from plants. It also helps in beautifying the plants 26 by cutting them into various shapes for growth. Pic 3.3 3. Garden Hoe A garden hoe is used to stir the soil, plant, seeds and remove the debris. It is widely used in the kitchen garden and vegetable gardens. Pic 3.4
4. Lawn mower Lawn mower is used to keep the green grass in the gardens at uniform height. By this, greenery can be maintained and the garden can be well cared. Pic 3.5

5. Garden Rake Garden Rake is a tool to remove leaves and twigs. It also helps in levelling the soil surface by spreading it evenly. 6. Watering Can Pic 3.6 Watering can is used to irrigate plants. The Pic 3.7 required quantity of water can be supplied with it. 7. Wheelbarrow Wheelbarrow is used to transport heavy objects like soil, manure, small rocks etc from one place to another easily. Pic 3.8 8. Secateur Secateur is used for making pencil thick cuttings and also for 27 pruning the braches of plants. Pic 3.9 9. Hand Trowel A hand trowel is used to dig the soil in small areas, and to uproot seedlings without damaging the roots. Pic 3.10 10. Shovel Used for lifting the soil Pic 3.11 Maintenance of farm tools is very important and these tools should be kept clean after use and used as and when needed.

Different Stages of Garden Making Even when you plant a small seedling, do you think of the day when it will grow into a big tree? Likewise, commence making a garden that evokes the beauty of nature. It will be the beginning of a fun journey of experience and happiness. 1. Finding a suitable site Getting a suitable site is an important factor in gardening. A site with well drained fertile soil that gets enough sunlight and water for plants is the best. It is best to equip the available space. In some places rather than changing the existing obstacles, they can be retained and transformed into elements of beauty. Maintain existing shade trees as much as possible. The garden location should be in such a way that a good view of the garden can be obtained from the corridor of the building.

2. Garden layout and Design Irrespective of the location and type of garden, a layout must be prepared first. To make a good garden it must be well designed. A plan should first be made as to how to divide the space within the garden and where to place the necessary components for the garden. First of all a garden layout should be drawn on a paper detailing the division of space. The placement of garden components should be noted on the layout. Entrance gate, main avenues, pathways, trees, hedges, border, edges and the shrubs should be marked on the layout. If more space is allocated for the lawn, in the final stage, if necessary, it can be used for other components. Ensure the source of water for the garden while designing the layout.

1. Arch 4. Flower Bed 7. Topiary 10. Rosary 2. Lawn 5. Rock Garden 8. Aquatic Garden 11. Edge 3. Hedge 6. Tree 9. Statue 3. Land preparation 29 The soil should be ploughed or stirred well and all stones and stumps should be removed. The soil should be made fertile by adding necessary organic manures. Slopy lands can be divided into different layers and then levelled to make it attractive. 4. Selection of plants At this stage, you can decide what kind of plants you want. Some people prioritize flowering plants while others focus on foliage plants and fruit plants. Select suitable plants according to the climate and nature of the soil.. 5. Planting Seedlings should be transplanted from pots and nursery beds when there is moisture in soil. It is beautiful to plant the shrubs and trees in rows. Pits should be taken according to the size of seedlings to be planted. 6. Irrigation Water is very important for plants. Irrigate them regularly.

7. Care and Maintenance Proper care is required to maintain the beauty of the garden. The garden should always be kept clean. Regular pruning and removal of dried leaves and plants should be done. Add required fertilizers in proper time. Maintain moisture in the soil by mulching. Hedges should be trimmed regularly once they reach the desired height. Weeds should be removed in time. Lawns, edges of flower beds, pathways, hedges etc should be trimmed regularly. Seeds that are fallen from plants and trees must be removed at once or it will sprout from there. Pest and diseases should be controlled when identified. If there is no other way, make use of chemical pesticides. Foliar application of fertilizers is good for flowering plants. Home Garden : Fragrant Filled Area Do you know how important it is to have a beautiful garden in front of your home? A garden in front of your home is an area that brings joy to all irrespective of age. Beautiful flowers and greenery create a visual spectacle. Let us make out each component from selecting the suitable locality, up to the arrangement of plants and pathways. Pic 3.12 Home garden Things to give importance while designing a home garden Dividing the area: Divide the total area into two. Front area : Lawn for beauty and delight, ornamental plants, trees, flower beds, pathways, children's playarea. Sides and back area : Fruit trees, vegetable crops. Provide some open area in the backyard. Design: Garden can be designed according to the availability of land in home. Boundary setting: Make use of hedge plants for boundaries if there is no compound wall.

Importance of lawn: Make lawn as the main component while planting. Design of pavement and Paths: Prepare edges with plant or other materials for pavements and paths. Arrangement of Flowerbeds Prepare flower beds on both sides of the path. Plant Hides High walls, untidy areas and slabs can be hided by planting shrubs. Activity 4 Using readily available materials and decorative plants, students can design and create ornamental gardens in small backyard spaces. Document the process of garden making and present it in the class. 32 Conclusion Ornamental gardens serve more than just aesthetic purposes. They help strengthen our bond with nature, promote environmental conservation, and contribute to mental well-being and enjoyment. By engaging in such activities, we not only develop a love for the environment, but also gain a sense of fulfilment and improved mental health. Indoor gardening

Indoor gardening is a method of growing ornamental plants in houses, offices and other closed places. For this small balcony or space near windows are enough. Indoor gardens can also be created by planting ornamental plants or flowering plants in miniature pots. People give more importance to indoor gardening in today's world due to lack of space, lack of time, less care and a healthy environment. Apart from giving coldness to the mind, indoor plants create greenery and increase the beauty of the house and improve the quality of air. Snake plant, money plant, zz plant, etc are suitable for indoor plants.

Green Bloomed Lawn What is a Lawn? Have you seen soft green lawn in the premises of your school, park or sports ground? Lawn is a green carpet trimmed out using some kind of special grass in place of garden, home, park, office premises, public places etc. It is a place of greenery protected for happiness and entertainment in the garden. Pic 3.13 Features of lawn Increases the attractiveness of garden. Helps in maintaining the coolness of the environment. It is a good place for entertainment and relaxation for children and adults. It can be used as a proper place for some physical training. (pitch/court/turf) 33 It helps to prevent wind and dust. Lawn Making : Do you know how important it Pic 3.14 is to prepare soil for a beautiful and healthy lawn? For that, give attention to the following things. Selection of land Non-shady places getting good sunlight is ideal for lawn making.

Land Preparation The soil should be ploughed to a depth of one a half feet, should be crushed and levelled well. Remove the roots, stem and tubers of weeds from the soil. Normally soil preparation is done in summer. Getting sunlight Exposing the soil to sunlight for 1-2 weeks destroy weeds and pests from the soil.

Fertilizer Application Organic manures are not needed for the fertile soil. Add 500kg of biofertilizers to 100 square metre of less fertile soil. Well dried and powdered organic manure should be added to the soil evenly. Consolidation of the soil Allow some time to consolidate the recently ploughed soil. In rainy areas after the first rain itself, soil will be consolidated. Irrigation of soil is necessary in places where there is scarcity of rain. Soil consolidation process should be repeated 2 - 3 times for consolidating the soil. Irrigate the soil and remove the weeds as and when they germinate. Shape and height of the lawn Lawn may not be even always; scenic beauty will be there when the lawn is 34 uneven. Pay attention that water filled ditches are not there. Planting method: Lawns can be prepared in many ways: mainly there are four methods 1. Sowing the seed 2. Turfing 3. Turf plastering 4. Dibbling
Turfing process Turfing: Turfing is the quickest method of lawn making. It is an interesting way of developing a green land by joining small pieces of lawn. Pic 3.15

Turfs are pieces of earth with compact grasses of 5 cm thickness. Turf are cut uniformly in squares from places where they are grown. Special attention should be given to avoid weeds. Spread the turfs on the prepared land side by side. Gaps in between should be filled with fine soil. Uneven land should be levelled by adding soil. It is good to spread bone meal early (a few days before planting). Fix the lawn using handled wooden mallet. Then irrigate the lawn liberally. In this method, the lawn can be made in a short time. Care and Maintenance of Lawn 1. Mowing : Mowing is the method of cutting grass in a lawn periodically. Usually this is done using the equipment lawn mower. Mowing is done to a height of 5 to 6 cm. It 35 is better to do mowing once in 2 to 3 weeks. 2. Rolling : Periodic levelling with a roller is beneficial to keep the grass in the soil firm and to protect the turf levelled. 3.

Weeding : Ensure weeding at regular intervals after making a lawn. Pic 3.16 4. Irrigation: Pour enough water daily to keep the lawn wet. 5. Fertilizer Application: Add organic or nutritious fertilizers once in 6 months. 6. Plant Protection : Spray pesticides if pests are formed in the grass. Pesticides can be used to destroy termites.

Miyawaki Forest Miyawaki forest represents an idea of creating a natural forest in a maximum period of 30 years instead of its inherent period of formation which is between 150 to 200 years. By planting native trees both small and big Miyawaki forests are created in cities. By planting three to four plants which includes big trees of two and a half feet,medium sized trees,small plants and shrubs in an area of 36 1 sq.metre over four layers is the most common method. Special Garden Features In the new era, new methods and styles are emerging to nurture ornamental plants more interestingly and easier. Kokedama, Terrarium, Miniature Garden etc are efforts to embrace the beauty of nature. Through this unit let's get familiarised with how we can shape the infinite beauty of nature with our hands and how to use these arts to bring joy to our loved ones and home. When we see the features of kokedama, terrarium and miniature garden, gardening seems to be an art form. Kokedama: A beautiful garden in a moss ball Kokedama is a Japanese style of gardening art. Growing plant in a ball of moss is the main idea in this ancient method where “koke” means “moss” and “dama” means “ball”. Kokedama is not only an interesting way to grow plant without using a pot, but also an art form. Today this is a very popular method for those who aspire for indoor gardening. Characteristics of Kokedama 1.

Moss ball: In Kokedama, roots of the plant are kept tightly inside a moss ball. 2. Jute Twine: Jute, fibre or other natural products are used to tie the roots tightly without touching the moss ball. This can be placed on the wall, in the corner of the room or on the table.

3.Sphagnum Moss: This is a growing media which helps to retain the essential moisture for the plant. 4.Potless Garden: The main feature of Kokedama is that it is an art form of growing plants without a pot. The lack of pot make kokedama different from other traditional garden forms. 5.Very low maintenance: It is easier to maintain Kokedama. For its proper care, make sure that it gets good light and water regularly. How to prepare Kokedama 1.Prepare the materials Plant (Choose a plant that is small and does not require much care. eg. Fern, succulents) Potting mixture Sphagnum Moss Jute twine ( or other natural fibre ) water 40 Pic 4.2 2. Prepare the ball: To make a ball of four inches, mix two cups of potting mixture with water. When the ball is ready, hold the ball with two hands and make a small hole on top of the ball. 3.

Prepare the plant: Take the plant from the polythene cover and carefully remove the potting mixture without damaging the roots. Place carefully into the hole of the ball. 4. Wrap and tie around: Wrap the ball with a sphagnum moss sheet. Tie the moss sheet with a waxed twine to keep the moss sheet in place. The round should be tied from the bottom of the ball to all directions. After tying around, the moss ball can be hung or placed in a pot. 5.Place under light: Kokedama can be hung in the wall or can be placed in a wide pot on a table. The plant should be placed in a place to get good light but not in direct sunlight.

6.Irrigation: Irrigation should be done as the weight of the ball decreases. For this, balls can be placed in a small bowl filled with water for 5 to 10 minutes. This has to done once in two weeks. Water soluble fertilizers can be added while irrigating. Features of Kokedama The attractive structure of kokedama gives indigenous visual spectacle and creates beautiful environment. The other important advantage of this is that it can be easily maintained. Besides, by giving a small touch of nature to the interior gives mental peace and relaxation. With the help of kokedama, we can make a beautiful indoor garden. This will give an experience that is different from the traditional one. Activity 1 Prepare a Kokedama by collecting necessary 41 materials. Terrarium : A small garden inside a glass container. Terrarium is a small garden growing in a glass container. Pic 4.3

It is a beautiful creation which can be kept inside a home or classrooms. Small and self reliant garden can be made using glass container. Hence it is beautiful like an art and can be easily maintained. Features of Terrarium 1. Small and beautiful garden: Terrarium is growing plants of greenery inside a glass container. This is suitable to be placed on a table or almirah in the house.

2. Self reliant ecosystem:Terrarium creates a self reliant ecosystem. All factors necessary for the growth of plants will be there in the small ecosystem inside the container. This can be maintained for a long period, as the water evaporates, condenses and re- irrigates the soil. 3. Less care: The plants in terrarium does not need much care. This sustains without pouring water for a short period. This is suitable for those who cannot spend more time in home. 4. A good decoration: Terrarium can be beautifully decorated using plants and structures in different kinds of glass containers. The size and shape of the containers can be varied. This can be designed as a way that is liked by anyone. How can we make Terrarium 1.

Preparation of materials : Glass container (closed or open ) Small plants (succulents, cactus or small leaved plants) Small stones, soil, coco peat, powdered cow dung, value added fertilizers etc 42 Small rocks, structure, stones, wooden pieces etc for decoration. 2. Preparation of container: Firstly, put small stones in the bottom of the container. This helps in draining the excess water. 3. Putting layers of soil: Layers of soil can be placed above the stones. Soil can be made fertile by mixing coco peat, powdered cow dung and organic manures. Ensure the drainage capacity of the soil. 4. Planting: Small plants can be planted in the prepared soil. Succulents, small cactus etc are plants suitable for terrarium. Fix the plant well along with the roots. 5.The beauty of the terrarium can be increased by adding small rocks and other decorative items above the soil. This will give terrarium the appearance of a small beautiful world.

6. Spray water: Try to keep the moisture of the soil by spraying enough water. Water should not be poured directly, but provide required water only. 7. Provide light: Place the terrarium in the area where sunlight is available. Direct sunlight should not be allowed.Plants grow well if sunlight is provided well. Use of Terrarium As terrarium is a decoration for home and class rooms, it can be placed on the table or almirah. It needs less care and it is small and convenient. It needs less irrigation and a little light. Moreover, Terrarium helps children to understand the importance and functions of environment by creating a small ecosystem. Conclusion Though Terrarium is a small garden creation inside Pic 4.4 43 a container, it is a beautiful art inside a house. As it needs less care, everyone can maintain and enjoy the beauty of it. Activity 2

Prepare an eco friendly Terrarium in a glass bowl using available natural materials. Miniature Garden: A small and beautiful garden. Miniature Garden is a small and an attractive garden. This is like creating a replica of a garden using small plants and decorative materials. Miniature Garden is a very special Pic 4.5 garden art. Because it gives opportunity to exhibit everyone's creative skills.

Features of a Miniature Garden 1.Small and attractive garden: Miniature Garden is a small and attractive garden created in a container or a small place. A small world can be made in this using small plants, structures, small statues and stones. 2. Open place or bowl : Miniature Garden can be placed on the floor or on the table or on the balcony. This is suitable as an ornamental garden along with a big garden. 3. Use of decorative items: Small structures, rocks, small furniture, small pathways, flowers etc can make a Miniature Garden more attractive. This is an art. A fantasy world can be created by the proper construction of Pic 4.6 garden components. 44 4. Small plants Small plants succulents, small flowering plants etc are mainly used in a Miniature Garden. They need less care. How can we make a Miniature Garden 1.

Preparation of materials: Soil (good irrigation capacity and fertile) small pots (attractive containers that you can use for making a garden) small plants (succulents, cactus, plants having small flowers) Small statues, furniture, rocks, decorative items 2. Land preparation: Firstly, fill the soil in the pot having miniature garden or on the floor. Include stones. under the soil for easy irrigation. After that, soil must be spreaded evenly.

3. Planting of small plants: Plants suitable for Miniature Garden,eg: Succulents, plants having small flowers etc can be planted in the soil in the pot or on the floor. 4. Add decoratives A small world can be framed using small statues, structures, rocks and small decoratives. An imaginary world can be created by arranging them as you like it. 5. Spray water: Give enough water for plants. Pay attention not to pour little or more water in small containers. Small plants doesnt need more water. 6. Provide light Place the Miniature Garden in a place which receives moderate light. Direct sunlight should be avoided as it may be harmful to plants. Advantages of Miniature Garden Miniature Garden is a beautiful idea which can be constructed and maintained easily inside and outside a home. This gives attraction to the garden and provides 45 art forms and visible features. Maintenance is easy as it is small.

A little effort only is needed to keep it as necessary water and sunlight is provided. Conclusion Miniature Garden is not only an interesting method of making a small and beautiful garden, but also a chance to give plants an opportunity to live in a small place in a home.

Tea Cup Garden Tea Cup Garden is an imaginary Miniature Garden. The speciality of this is growing small and beautiful plants in old tea cups. Usually plants which need less care including succulants, cactus etc are used for this. This is suitable as an attractive decoration idea for home and to add a touch of greenery. Pic 4.7

Activity 3 Make a Miniature Garden using available materials including some garden components. New garden constructions, combining contemporary and aesthetic sense, opens up new arena to nurture the presence of nature, even in the modern life with limited space. Contemporary garden making practices such as Miniature Garden, Terrarium, Kokedama etc, which are discussed in this unit, may create eco friendly and creative spaces. These practices, which gives very little effort for irrigation, maintenance etc, satisfies aesthetic sense also. Moving Ahead Prepare and exhibit different shapes of Terrarium, Kokedama and Miniature Garden. Mawlynnong has earned the prestigious title of being the cleanest village in Asia. How did Mawlynnong, an inland village in Meghalaya, catch the attention of the public? In the eastern hills of Meghalaya, Mawlynnong was a quiet and beautiful village inhabited by the indigenous Khasi tribe. For generations, they lived a simple life, in harmony with nature without much contact with the outside world. In course of time, the association of village people and governing bodies worked together and thereby brought the village's cultural values of cleanliness, sustainable living and social cooperation to the attention of the world. This village's dedication to cleanliness and sustainable living earned Mawlynnong the prestigious title of 'Asia's Cleanest Village' in 2003, an international recognition by Discover India magazine. This status has made the village a tourism destination.
Tourists still flock to Mawlynnong for its stunning scenery, bamboo walkways, flower-filled streets and nearby 'Living Root Bridges'.

This region has become a marketable tourism product by providing tourist facilities and promoting traditionally handed-down cultural values. You have read how a small village, Mawlynnong, became a tourism product. What facilities and preparations the locals prepared for the tourists? Write it down

The 7Ps of Marketing Once the market is known, marketing strategies can be formulated. The 7Ps of Marketing are the factors that influence marketing and the market. Pic 2.4 1. Product 23 When you are about to go on a trip, how will you find out the places to stay, restaurants, etc.? Most travellers choose the facilities they need by reading reviews from online sites. Therefore, customer 'reviews' about products are of utmost value to tourism service providers. Other customers come to them based on reviews. Price Will you compare the packages of different tour operators while planning a trip? Which factor will be compared first?

Everyone chooses products according to their financial capacity. While travelling, everyone's goal is to choose the best and most cost-effective travel options. Therefore, the price of the product and packages is a very important factor in marketing. 3. Place Pic 2.6 Where can you find information about travel packages when you plan a trip? Where did you get the information about the destination and accommodation? 24 The marketing place is an important factor in tourism marketing. 2. Street vendors Consider using eco-friendly products e.g. banana leaves. 3. Hotel/Homestay Notice boards should be placed in all rooms on what to do with the waste generated by the residents. Hazardous waste such as batteries and fluorescent lamps, CFL should be collected separately and disposed safely. Reduce the use of single-use plastic products. Encourage consumers to reduce and segregate waste. 4. Fruit/Juice Parlours/Ice Cream Vendors Promote the sale of ice creams with plastic-free packaging. Use only reusable straws 5. Boat / Houseboat / Coracle boat There should be a facility for sorting and collecting waste inside the boat.

It should be ensured that passengers or staff do not throw any kind of waste into the water body from the boats. Notices regarding the disposal of waste generated by tourists should be displayed on boats, quay, and ticket counters. Sanitary waste generated in boats with sanitation facilities should be disposed off in a scientific manner. There should be bins for segregating and collecting waste at the points where passengers board and disembark from the boats.

Packaging rules • Food Safety and Standards Act (FSSAI) : The FSSAI regulates food safety practices and provides consumers with safety assurances and knowledge to choose wholesome food products. It is mandatory to have a detailed labelling on food packaging, including ingredients, allergen warnings, nutritional content, and expiry/best-before dates. • Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 : These rules mandate the standardization of product information on packages, including the Maximum Retail Price (MRP), manufacturer details, total quantity, and customer helpline.

• Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 : These rules prohibit single- use plastics and implement Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for managing plastic waste. It also promotes biodegradable and compostable packaging.

• Consumer Protection Act, 2019 : This Act mandates transparent packaging with clear information on origin, ingredients, and health impacts. • The Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Packaging and Labelling) Rules, 2008: These Rules mandate that health warnings and graphic images, that aim at discouraging consumption, should cover 85% of the packaging space. • "Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) : Packaging must ensure hygiene and safety. The BIS prescribes quality and safety standards for packaging, particularly for food and pharmaceutical products. • Environment Protection Act, 1986 : This Act provides guidelines for handling hazardous substances in packaging, emphasizing the use of environment friendly materials, proper labelling, and safe disposal.

• The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 : This Act of the Indian Parliament regulates the manufacture, import, and distribution of drugs. Pharmaceutical and cosmetic packaging must ensure that drugs 14 and cosmetics sold in India are safe, effective, and meet the country's standards of quality. FOREWORD Dear Children, We are journeying through an era of constant changes, where new kinds of technologies are emerging every day. You will step into a new world completely different from the one you entered when you began your studies. We are surrounded by new knowledge wherever we go. While it is not at all difficult to discover this knowledge, it is necessary to gain expertise in certain professional fields if we are to survive in this new world. The scientific method involves forming new ideas, acquiring skills and abilities to implement them, and then testing them. Therefore, while learning various subjects is important, you should also create opportunities to gain in-depth knowledge and experience in your areas of interest. This is the aim of vocational education. There are various opportunities to get acquainted with various skill sets and engage in practical activities integrated with other subjects from grade five onwards.

The activity books are designed so that in Grade 9, students can focus more on their area of interest, participate in related activities, and gain skills. Activity books for Grade 10 are designed to help students explore career opportunities and higher education options and decide on a preliminary path after general education. The activity books are available in eleven areas, including Printing and Stationery- Printing and Packaging, Agriculture- The Science of Harvest, Media and Entertainment- Media Skills: Learn and Acquire, Food Industry- The World of Flavors, Electrical and Electronics- EC-Tronics, Finance- Financial Literacy, Housing- Basic Ideas of Constructing Houses, Clothing - Passion in Fashion, Tourism- Tourism and Hospitality, Green Technology - Green Technology Solutions for Waste Management and Plumbing- Pipes and Fittings: A Guide to Plumbing.

With the help of the activity book on Food Industry - The World of Flavors, you can learn about the skills, job opportunities, and study areas in this industry. This book will inspire you to advance by recognizing the importance of knowledge and its application in the context of current changes. Warm regards,

No. Dish Cooking Methods Utensils 1 Puttu Steamed Puttu maker Culinary Varieties Cooking is an art of preparing food in different temperature and at different ways. (Remember there are dishes that are prepared without cooking). It is possible to 8 adjust the level of heat to make the dishes tastier in different cooking methods. Have you ever thought of the heat absorption during cooking? Food can be cooked using all three methods of heat transfer–Conduction, Convection and Radiation. How do you prepare food at home? Let us explore two cooking methods and the heat absorption in these methods.

Conduction Conduction is a cooking method using a metal pan or pan with direct heat from the stove. e.g. Making dosa Convection Convection is a method of cooking food in boiling water or steam. Here heat from boiling water is transferred to the food. e.g. Preparation of rice or idli Radiation Radiation refers to the transfer of heat through electromagnetic waves. In this process, heat is transferred directly to the food without needing a medium like air or water. e.g. Preparation of food using Microwave

Dry-heat method The dry heat method in cooking involves transferring heat to food directly or indirectly by adding a little water. Instead, heat is applied directly to the food or indirectly through hot air or a heated surface. In dry heat methods, conduction and radiation are the 11 two main modes of heat transfer. A. Organise a food fest by preparing a variety of dishes that cover all cooking methods. 13 Changes in food during heating Food contains protein, fat, carbohydrates, water, minerals, vitamins and flavour components. When heated or mixed together, certain elements essential for the body can alter the quality of food. Temperature adjustment helps retain nutrients. Note the change in nutrients when food is cooked at different temperature. Proteins l The major component in meat, fish, egg and milk is protein. Beans ,lentils and grains also contains less amount of protein.
l Proteins become firm and solid when heated. As the temperature rises, they shrink, firm and lose its moisture. e.g. Boiled eggs l The connective tissues in meat contains proteins.

Carbohydrates l Starch and sugar are carbohydrates. Both components are found in food in various forms. Carbohydrates are found in larger amounts in vegetables, fruits and grains and lesser amount in lentils and meat. l The two most important changes in carbohydrates caused by heat are Caramelisation and Jelatinisation. Caramelisation is a process that occurs when sugar is heated until it breaks down and turns brown. Outer brown layer of bread or loaves are also forms of Caramelisation. Gelatinisation is a process in which starch granules absorb water and swell when heated in the presence of water. Sauces and puddings are prepared through Gelatinisation. Fibres of Fruits and Vegetables The fibres are complex substance that provides structure and strength to fruits and vegetables. 14 Fat l Meat, fish, egg and milk products contain large amount of fat. Reduce the amount of oil while cooking food items.

l Fat exists in the form of solids or liquids in atmospheric temperature. Liquid fats are different types of oils. Butter, cheese, ghee etc are fats in solid form. Minerals, Vitamins, Pigments l Minerals and vitamins add nutritional values to food while pigments add co- lour to it. l All these components leach or dissolve from the food during cooking. l The vitamins and pigments are lost due to overcooking. l It is important to choose cooking methods that preserve as much of the nutrients and benefits of food as possible.

Fusion cuisine is a cooking method that combines elements of different culinary traditions originating from various countries, regions, or cultures. It does not require fixed ingredients or measurements. Fusion dishes have been available in our restaurants for years. Have you included fusion dishes in the menu card you prepared? Which are they?

18 Look at the picture, how many of you know that Gobi Manchurian, which we enjoy eating so much, is a fusion dish? The fried Cauliflower is an Indian dish, and the spices added are Chinese. Thus Gobi Manchurian is an Indo- Chinese fusion dish.

Features of Fusion Cuisine Having travelled the world and tasted countless cuisines, a traveller was inspired to create a unique culinary experience by combining the best flavours from around the globe. Each taste touched his heart. The traveller decided to fulfil his dream by the inspiration he imbibed from his journey. What would happen if the flavours from different corners of the world were combined? Fusion dishes help us explore and learn about different cultures and traditions. By preparing fusion dishes, we can experiment with different flavours and cooking methods. Fusion cuisine can attract food lovers by combining familiar and unique ingredients. What if we try to present a unique taste of experience?

Integrated Circuit (IC) Electronic components such as Diodes, Transistors, Capacitors and Resistors are automatically incorporated in a small semi conductor chip is called Integrated Circuit (IC). With the invention of IC, size of the electronic equipments could be reduced significantly. Transistor A transistor is a semiconductor device used to amplify or regulate electronic signals and intensity of electric current. Transistors ensure that devices in a circuit receive the necessary voltage. Transistors also help to regulate the electric current through a circuit, ensuring that excess electric current is prevented, which reduces the risk of damage to equipment. As one of the fundamental building blocks of modern electronics, transistors play a vital role in devices such as computers, radios, mobile phones, and televisions. There are two types of transistors 1. npn transistor 2. pnp transistor

Relay module Relay modules serve as interface device that enable the transfer of signals and information between different devices or systems. They act as a bridge, allowing low powered digital electronic devices such as micro controllers, Arduino and Raspberry Pi, to control high powered devices like motors, lighting circuit etc. Hope you have understood the symbols of various electronic components and their uses. How to reduce electricity consumption One of the most important research activities related to electricity is to find devices that minimize the consumption of electricity. The results of these types of investigations led to the shift from incandescent bulbs to LED bulbs. Fan is one of the devices that increase electricity consumption in homes. BLDC fans have an efficiency of 80% to 90%, whereas fans with conventional motors have only 40% to 60% efficiency. 2.

Using electronic regulator The consumption of electricity can also be reduced by using an electronic regulator instead of resistor type regulators. There are basically three types of Electronic Regulators based on Circuits. 1. Variable resistor circuit

Materials needed Holder – 1 1½ sq mm wire – 6 metre (3 m red, 3 m black) Two pin plug – 1 LED bulb – 1 Probes – 2 ( Red, black)

Unit Water Conservation 2 Pic. 2.1 This picture shows the present condition of two roads that were completed at the 13 same time. Why is the road in the second picture damaged? What problems will arise if the roads are flooded due to the rains which occur six month in an year? Why is the road in the first picture undamaged? A proper drainage system exists. When it rains, water from nearby places and houses flows onto roads. If water stagnates in houses or fields, it can lead to serious health issues. It can also cause damage to buildings. Well recharging is one of the methods adopted in our homes to avoid water stagnation and other related issues. How many houses use this method ? In most houses and institutions, water is usually drained out and wasted. The scarcity of water to some extent can be avoided by reusing and collecting water at
a specific location. There are various methods in different parts of the world that, scientifically collect, treat, and reuse rainwater and wastewater from homes.

Dual Pipeline System A dual pipeline system is a water management system that uses two pipelines to distribute different types of water for different purposes.This system is designed to promote efficient water consumption and reduce unnecessary usage of water. The speciality of this method is that rainwater is collected in large rainwater tanks in institutions or homes and the excess water can be drained through a specially designed public pipe, where it can be collected, purified, and used for drinking purposes. Another advantage of the dual pipe line system is that the wastewater coming from the toilet (except the wastewater from the septic tank) and wastewater from the kitchen can also be collected, stored, and treated through a separate pipe, and then used for the water requirements of the flush tank in the houses, institutions, industries etc.
We can build and maintain this type of model in places where drinking water sources are scarce, considering the possibility of a decrease in the availability of 14 drinking water in the future.
This practice exists both in India and abroad. Pic 2.2

In the ERW / EFW / HFW pipe process, the plate is first formed into a cylindrical shape. The ends of the cylinder are then welded using one of the following methods: flash welding, low frequency resistance welding, high frequency induction welding, or high frequency resistance welding. Gas & Oil Pipe Dimensions 32 There are several criteria for calculating pipe dimensions. 1. Pipe Thickness

Pipe thickness is expressed in schedule number. The schedule number is calculated using the formula 1000P/S, where P stands for service pressure and S stands for allowable stress. Common schedule numbers are 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, and 160. The higher the schedule number, the thicker the pipe and the smaller the inner diameter. Pipe thickness is also expressed as Standard-STD, Extra Strong - XS, Double Extra Strong - XXS, etc.

Pipe Length The length of a pipe is indicated in meters or feet. During production, pipes are not made in the same length. For the construction of process plants, pipes of different lengths are required. To solve this problem, pipe lengths are categorized as standard in single random and double random lengths. Single random pipe is available in lengths ranging from 4.8 m to 6.7 m (5% of pipes can be 3.7 m to 4.8 m in length). Double random pipe has a minimum average length of 10.7 m (5% of pipes can be 4.8 m to 10.7 m in length). Pipes can also be ordered in fixed lengths, but this will increase the cost. 3. Pipe Ends

Pipe ends are available in 4 types. Plain End - Used for socket type weld fittings. Beveled End - Used for butt type weld fittings. Threaded End - Used for threaded connections in piping systems Socket & Spigot - Used in ductile iron pipe and in non-metallic piping pipelines. Pipes should be selected based on dimensions such as pipe thickness, pipe length, and pipe ends.

UNIT Natural Resources are not Limitless Through previous lessons, you have learned that things that are no longer necessary are not just wastes but still hold value as materials. You have also learned to convert organic/biodegradable wastes into bio fertilizers and bio gas, rendering them harmless. Now, if we also recognise a recycling method for non-biodegradable wastes, we can achieve a state of zero waste. This workbook aims to prepare you for that. Have you ever wondered how different kinds of commodities negatively affect nature? Observe Picture 1.1 Pic 1.1 The manufacturing of commodities through uncontrolled exploitation of natural resources and the indiscriminate production of toxic wastes threaten

the security of the Earth. Reclaiming materials from waste and recycling them continually is the solution to this. It is also important to organize our lifestyle accordingly. Deployment of Toxin Metal ions and compounds, as well as some organometallic compounds, can be produced from product residues, and these are extremely harmful. Non- metals like bromine and fluorine are also included in this group. When hard metals turn into ions, they are converted into deadly poisons. The severity of this is proportional to the quantity as well, Pic 1.2 and their ability to accumulate is even more dangerous. The impact of the habit of neglecting metallic objects can be 8 passed on from generation to generation.

Microplastic Deployment The alarming presence of micro plastics is one reason why plastic debris is more harmful. Plastic fibres less than five millimetres long can penetrate living cells and destroy them. Micro plastics can wreak similar havoc not only on the marine biosphere but also on the terrestrial ecosystem. The scale of the impact of plastic deployment on the life-supporting system is not trivial. 1.1 Commodity and Source The source of human-made commodities is the Earth’s resources. The main non-biodegradable natural resources are metal ores, fossil fuels, and minerals. They exist as mixtures of compounds in their pristine state, and human beings have acquired the knowledge to transform and utilise them since ancient times. Many commodities can be made from one single material, and many materials can make one single commodity.

How can materials be recovered from commodities? First, the correlation between the materials and the commodities should be identified. Try the following practical activity. Analysis There are mainly two categories that satisfy all the qualities mentioned in the table above- metals and polymer resins. Both are derived from natural resources. 2.3. Diversity in Plastic Products The resins produced in massive quantities include polymers like polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinyl, polystyrene, and polyurethane. Refer to Pic 2.3. Each of these resins is transformed into plastics by adding additional substances, such as plasticisers. The physical and chemical properties, including material quality, behaviour, and lifespan, vary across these resins. These differences enabled the production of numerous types of plastics from each resin. Consequently, the market became flooded with diverse plastic products. Pic 2.3

• What type of resin is used in the plastic product being purchased? • Can it be used to store food? • Can it hold boiling substances? • Is it microwave-safe? • Can it be stored in a deep freezer? Such questions have emerged in the market. To meet specific needs, plastic products are now made from multiple resins. Market need for plastic was soon engineered. Instead of manufacturing plastic solely for necessity, an artificial demand was created. However, a serious issue arose: if waste plastic needs to be recycled to recover resin, identifying the type of resin used in its manufacture becomes essential. This is crucial because many resins cannot be

processed together, and hence, it became necessary for each plastic product to have an identification tag. To solve the above-mentioned problem, the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, mandated that everyone must understand the recycling resin numbers and associated symbols. Activity 3

We are not careful enough regarding the use of plastic products. Carrying hot rice wrapped in plastic sheets or storing food items in unsuitable plastic containers, pouches, or bottles is harmful to health. This is because plastic fibers or metal content in plasticizers may contaminate the food. When milk packets are stored in deep freezers, the plastic cover can freeze, break into microfibers, and mix with the milk. Taking such frozen packets and putting them in boiling water is also not a safe practice. Milk and dairy products should be stored in deep-freezer-friendly plastic cups or containers. Recycled plastic products should not be used for handling food items. Such low-cost containers and banned carry bags must not be used, as they are not suitable for handling food.

3D Printing Compatibility: A New Path for Recycling A 3D printer is a device that converts computer models (digital designs) into three-dimensional objects. There are various types of printers, in which the most common type uses melted plastic filament for 21 deposition. In this method, polymers are used in filament form wound on rolls. Observe the figure. The deposition of melted plastic corresponding to the design created on the computer is carried out through a moving extruder. 3D printing is also possible by passing LED or laser beams through the molten plastic. Since the beams follow the design provided on the computer, they deposit the polymer in that shape, creating a three-dimensional object using this innovative method. Many plastics are compatible with 3D printing. Plastic bottles and containers that have reached the end of their usage period can be melted and converted into filament form for use in 3D printing.
This is an innovative recycling method. Plastics such as PLA, PET, PP, ABS, PC, and Nylon-6 are commonly used for 3D printing.

2.4. Single-Use Products: Non-Recyclable Problematic Materials Every individual is a consumer of plastic products. There is no debate that single-use plastics (SUP) are products meant for momentary use, commonly found at events, tourist spots, and other locations. The plastic market expanded under such circumstances. However, the concerning fact is that such disposable plastics account for nearly 50% of the total plastic production. Non-degradable plastic waste, which lasts for centuries, has started to destroy the land and oceans gradually. Large ecosystems like forests are also under threat. Various studies by United Nations environmental agencies reveal this reality (For detailed reading, refer to Annexure 1).

From January 1, 2023, single-use plastics have been banned. For carry bags, there is a complete prohibition on those with less than 150 microns thickness. Very thin packaging films are also now banned. Meanwhile, the shift towards a green lifestyle has significantly gained momentum. Considering such 22 contemporary developments, it is impossible to advance plastic studies without addressing these issues. Therefore, the following three key aspects can be examined through practical activities: • Understanding banned plastic products. • Manufacturing alternative plastic products (bio-plastics). • Manufacturing alternative plastic packaging (casein polymer film). Polymer Formation Starch consists of two forms: amylose (20-25%) and amylopectin (75-80%). Amylose has a comparatively higher solubility. When heated with water, the starch molecules absorb water, break apart, and form fine particles. At this stage, amylose easily combines with water and obtains a gel-like structure due to hydrogen bonding. Amylopectin then joins the fine particles, creating a fully viscous gel (gelatinization). After drying, when the water content reduces to about 13%, it gains strength. This indicates that thermoplastic starch (TPS) has been formed. Glycerine, acting as a plasticizer in this process, is included to provide flexibility. In industrial production, gelatin, a protein, is often added to this mixture. The accepted thickness of TPS films is 250 microns. 25 Activity 6

2.7. Sanitary Pad Management Proper disposal of sanitary pads presents significant challenges, particularly in schools. While many schools operate incinerators, the following issues are often encountered during their use: • Incinerators are not repaired when damaged. • Even after repairs, they frequently malfunction again. 34 • Excessive smoke and foul odours are emitted during operation. • Electricity costs are disproportionately high. • There is a lack of supervision and planning for collection and proper disposal. These issues are also common in homes and institutions to varying degrees. However, their severity often goes unnoticed because sanitary pads are frequently burned openly, typically along with other waste. This practice spreads unpleasant odours and smoke in the surrounding areas. Despite its prevalence, the impact on air pollution is often overlooked.

Hope you have read the above given things. What do you understand from this? • Safe disposal methods for sanitary pads are essential. • Burning pads openly and widely is an incorrect approach. • When such practices are widespread, toxic substances from the smoke and fumes significantly contaminate the air. • The toxic gases released from burning sanitary pads are similar to those emitted when plastic carry bags and other plastics are burned.

What is the Solution? Safe alternative products are certainly a step forward. However, it is unrealistic to assume that the use of sanitary pads can be entirely eliminated, especially given the prevalence of advertisements extolling their benefits. In this context, the following activities related to the management of sanitary pads can be undertaken. Burning and incinerating Experiment Required Materials • Unused baby diapers- 2 nos • Dry coconut shell (as needed) • Coconut husk (as needed) • Bricks/concrete blocks (any one, as needed) • Thermocouple thermometer • Mask and gloves

• Arrange the layers properly in the setup as shown in the diagram. • Place coconut husks and coconut shells in the pattern shown in the diagram. These are used to generate a flame for burning the pads. • Ignite it using a fireball or lighter. • Measure the flame temperature, maintaining it up to 200°C. • Place one diaper/pad on each of the two layers. • Ignite the diaper/pad on the first layer using a fireball. • Periodically measure and record the temperature on both layers. 36 • Observe and record the changes occurring in the diapers/pads. • Pay close attention to the colour variations in the ash. Observations • The burning or combustion process starts from atmospheric temperature. • Smoke is emitted during the transition phase, as the temperature rises past the melting point and approaches the fire point. • When diapers/pads are placed in the high-temperature flame after surpassing the melting and fire points, they burn completely.

This is called incineration. Combustion, followed by incineration, occurs as the materials, including the pyrolytic fuel gases burn entirely. This results in a noticeable rise in the furnace temperature. Conclusion • Starting the incinerator only after placing the diaper/pad is similar to burning, which produces smoke, indicating improper operation. • Operating the incinerator in advance to attain the required temperature and then placing the diaper/pad results in incineration without significant smoke or odour. This represents the proper operation of the incinerator.

If the above experiments involve attempting to burn pads instead of incinerating them, toxic fumes will be released during the gradual rise in temperature at the melting and subsequent burning points. Battery Recycling Lead-Acid Batteries Lead-acid batteries are categorized into four types. The commonly used Start Batteries and Storage Batteries belong to the FLA (Flooded Lead Acid) category. The second type includes sealed batteries with controlled casing (Sealed LA or Valve Regulated LA). The third type consists of batteries with a gel electrolyte, while the fourth type belongs to the Glass Mat category. These batteries are collected and mechanically (using a machine) shredded into small pieces. The sulphuric acid is neutralized, and plastic polymers are separated. The metal content is extracted. The outer casing is made 58 of polypropylene plastic. The primary metal is Lead, which is a toxic substance, commonly found in the form of lead oxide. This method involves separating and refining polypropylene and Lead, which are then sent to specialized recycling facilities.

Not all primary recycling centers are equipped with advanced purification machinery. Thus, the Lead and Lead oxide components are transported to centralized smelter furnaces, where they are melted, refined, and separated for reuse in new production. Similarly, the recycled polypropylene is sent to plastic manufacturing units, where it is either incorporated into new products at permissible levels or used exclusively for creating recycled plastic products.

Lithium-ion Batteries The goal of recycling Lithium-ion batteries is to recover basic metals like Cobalt, Nickel, and Copper, along with rare metals like Manganese and Lithium. There are different recycling methods: Pyrometallurgy: This involves melting the batteries in smelter furnaces to extract the metals. However, a drawback is that Lithium may vaporize at high temperatures, leading to loss. Advanced machinery is required to refine the resulting alloy and separate individual metals for reuse.

Hydrometallurgy: In this method, strong acids are used to dissolve the metal components into a solution. Metals are then recovered from the solution. Direct Recycling: This involves recovering cathode electrolytes from batteries without damage, allowing them to be reused for manufacturing new batteries. Alkaline Batteries The primary materials in alkaline batteries include Zinc, Manganese, Steel, paper, plastic, and Brass alloys. These are among the most commonly discarded small batteries, particularly in the form of alkaline dry cell batteries. The recycling method is similar to other battery types. UNIT 5 Recycling Industry: The New Economy Cautious use of resources is the goal of the circular economy. The cyclical process of retrieving raw materials from waste products and converting them back into commodities is literally nature's hand-me-down. It is an atonement for the pollution that the lavishness of the Take-Make-Use-Waste approach creates on Mother Nature, and Take-Make-Use-Recirculate will be the solution for the over exploitation of natural resources. Recirculation Technology and Economy is a primary development strategy of the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP). 5.1 Recycling Technology: Towards Sustainable Development

Manufacturing technologies used in both virgin and recycled products are similar. In both cases, the required machinery is essentially the same. The variations occur in manufacturing and groundwork. They are all related areas like collection, purification, and concentration. Sectors utilizing remanufactured products are expanding at an astonishing rate today. Advanced metal alloys (e.g., GRX-810), composite plastics (e.g., epoxy resins), and conductive plastics (e.g., poly acetylene) are just a few examples in this category. The recycling economy is driven by the development of material science technologies and the use of nanotechnology.

Recycling technologies and entrepreneurship in all three sectors – electronic equipment, batteries, and plastics – are interdependent and complementary.
